svg.text: Juice Shop · 20.0.0 · 8 components · 19 data flows · 3 trust boundaries (2 inferred) · 68 threats
acts on the pipeline, not on traffic

g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 External → C-02; tb-2 External → C-08; tb-3 C-02 → External

df-001: Express server delivers static Angular SPA bundle (JS/HTML/CSS) to browser on initial request (HTTP) df-001 authentication: Static asset delivery requires no authentication; evidence: server.ts:26

df-002: Unauthenticated REST API calls: product listing, user registration, login, captcha, public feedback (HTTP) df-002 authentication: No token checked; POST /api/Users and POST /api/Feedbacks lack auth middleware; evidence: server.ts:407, routes/verify.ts:113 df-002 access group: SPA to API (auth variant); alternatives; step n/a

df-003: Authenticated REST API calls with JWT Bearer token from localStorage; basket, orders, user profile (HTTP) df-003 authentication: JWT RS256 token from localStorage as Authorization: Bearer; verified by lib/insecurity.ts; evidence: frontend/src/app/Services/request.interceptor.ts:13, lib/insecurity.ts:158 df-003 access group: SPA to API (auth variant); alternatives; step n/a

df-004: Cookie-authenticated request for GDPR data erasure using session token cookie (HTTP) df-004 authentication: Session token cookie checked in routes/dataErasure.ts for GDPR erasure flow; evidence: routes/dataErasure.ts:76 df-004 access group: SPA to API (auth variant); alternatives; step n/a

df-005: Sequelize ORM queries: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on all relational models (users, products, orders) (Sequelize/SQLite) df-005 authentication: In-process library call; no network transport or credential required; evidence: models/index.ts:34

df-006: Login credential lookup and user record retrieval via Sequelize ORM in auth routes (Sequelize/SQLite) df-006 authentication: In-process library call; no separate credential for DB access; evidence: models/index.ts:34

df-007: MarsDB queries for product reviews and orders from chatbot and review routes (MarsDB) df-007 authentication: In-process library call; MarsDB runs in the same Node.js process; evidence: data/mongodb.ts:9

df-008: Browser Socket.IO WebSocket connection for challenge notifications and verification events (WebSocket) df-008 authentication: No authentication check; confirmed by T-016 (evidence-verified); evidence: lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:24
df-009: User input; evidence: frontend/src/app/app.guard.ts:17, frontend/src/app/app.routing.ts:162

df-012: POST /rest/user/login with email and password credentials; server validates and returns signed JWT (HTTP) df-013: POST /rest/2fa/verify with TOTP token during MFA step after initial password login (HTTP) df-012 authentication: Email and password submitted in request body; no existing session required; evidence: routes/login.ts:34 df-012 access group: Credentials (MFA if enrolled); sequence; step 1 df-013 authentication: Temporary token (totp_tmp_token) from password step plus TOTP code; sequence step 2 of login; evidence: routes/2fa.ts:31 df-013 access group: Credentials (MFA if enrolled); sequence; step 2

df-014: POST chat completion to OpenAI-compatible LLM API; user message in prompt via Vercel AI SDK (HTTPS) df-014 authentication: LLM provider API key configuration not verified in source; depends on deployment provider; evidence: routes/chat.ts:106

df-015: POST /file-upload: unauthenticated multipart file upload; no auth middleware on this route (HTTP) df-016: Unauthenticated GET /rest/admin/application-version and application-configuration endpoints (HTTP) df-017: POST /rest/chat: unauthenticated LLM chatbot; any caller sends messages without authentication (HTTP) df-015 authentication: Route has no authentication middleware; any unauthenticated caller can upload; evidence: routes/fileUpload.ts:19 df-016 authentication: No authentication middleware on admin info endpoints; decode_only signal present but no enforcement; evidence: routes/verify.ts:113 df-017 authentication: No authentication middleware on /rest/chat route; evidence: routes/verify.ts:113
df-019: User input; evidence: frontend/src/app/app.guard.ts:48, frontend/src/app/app.routing.ts:81, frontend/src/app/administration/administration.component.ts:73

Internet Attacker → C-01 · Authentication & Session Surface: scenario 1, 2; its findings also affect C-02 · Express.js REST API Backend, C-04 · SQLite Database (Sequelize ORM)
Internet Attacker → C-07 · Web3 / Wallet / NFT Surface: scenario 2, 3, 4
Internet Attacker → C-06 · Real-time WebSocket Channel: scenario 4
Internet Attacker → Juice Shop User: scenario 6, 7
Supply-Chain / Build Attacker → C-08 · CI/CD Pipeline: scenario 8
C-01 · Authentication & Session Surface: JWT Signing Key Pair
C-01 · Authentication & Session Surface: User Session Tokens (JWT)
Dynamic code evaluation — evidence: routes/userProfile.ts:61 (reported finding)
Further capabilities: XML parsing — evidence: routes/fileUpload.ts:83 (reported finding); Server-side templates — evidence: routes/userProfile.ts:87 (reported finding)
C-03 · Angular Web Application (SPA): User Session Tokens (JWT)
C-04 · SQLite Database (Sequelize ORM): User Credentials and Password Hashes
C-04 · SQLite Database (Sequelize ORM): User Personal Data (PII)
C-04 · SQLite Database (Sequelize ORM): Payment Card Data
C-04 · SQLite Database (Sequelize ORM): Challenge State and Progress Data
C-05 · MarsDB Embedded Document Store: Product Reviews and Order Documents
C-08 · CI/CD Pipeline: CI/CD Pipeline Configuration and Secrets
Human user operating a web browser to interact with the Juice Shop Angular SPA, including anonymous shoppers and registered users.

Google accounts.google.com OAuth 2.0 authorization server. The Angular SPA redirects users here for social login using the implicit grant (response_type=token). Returns an access token in the URL fragment.

External LLM inference endpoint: either an OpenAI-compatible remote API or a local Ollama instance (localhost:11434). Receives user chat messages from the Express chatbot route and returns generated responses.
g.text: API or a local Ollama instance…

g.title: Application role with elevated rights, evidenced by its access check.

Google OAuth Authorization Server df-010: Browser redirects to Google OAuth endpoint with response_type=token (implicit grant) for social login (HTTPS); OAuth 2.0 implicit grant; Angular SPA redirects browser to Google for authorization df-011: Google OAuth returns access token in URL fragment (#access_token=...) after implicit grant (HTTPS); Completes the sign-in: the provider returns its result to the client's registered redirect URI df-018: OAuth profile request (HTTPS); The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request

C-03 · Angular Web Application (SPA) df-010: Browser redirects to Google OAuth endpoint with response_type=token (implicit grant) for social login (HTTPS); OAuth 2.0 implicit grant; Angular SPA redirects browser to Google for authorization df-011: Google OAuth returns access token in URL fragment (#access_token=...) after implicit grant (HTTPS); Completes the sign-in: the provider returns its result to the client's registered redirect URI df-018: OAuth profile request (HTTPS); The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE-per-element: filled = threats found in that class
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
A1 ①② = scenarios of attacker A1 · A1 at an arrowhead = its attack
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
LLM + tools = model calls with executable application tools
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
finding; +N = further labels, listed under Further capabilities.
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
Matching E-labels indicate a connection; lines omitted.
Missing authorization grants admin and cross-user
User-controlled input executes as server-side code
Compromise the Build or Its Inputs
The recipient performs no authentication check on this connection.
The recipient checks the supplied password.
The recipient checks the token supplied with the request.
A session cookie identifies the caller.
Delegated access; only the evidenced protocol step is covered.
Temporary token (totp_tmp_token) from password step plus TOTP code;
Authentication could not be determined from the code.
Numbered hexagon: authentication · circle: attack scenario
Red: absent / unsafe · yellow: standard / limited · green: stronger
Method properties, not proof of a secure implementation.
